question.en: In financial goal setting, what does the letter "M" in the SMART acronym stand for?
question.ms: Dalam penetapan matlamat kewangan, apakah yang diwakili oleh huruf "M" dalam akronim SMART?

feedback.en: Correct! Goals must have specific quantifiable monetary amounts to track progress.
feedback.ms: Tepat! Matlamat mesti mempunyai jumlah wang tertentu untuk mengukur kemajuan.

feedback.en: M stands for Measurable.
feedback.ms: M bermaksud Boleh diukur (Measurable).

feedback.en: M stands for Measurable.
feedback.ms: M mewakili Measurable.

feedback.en: T represents Time-bound, M represents Measurable.
feedback.ms: T mewakili Tempoh masa, M mewakili Boleh diukur.

en: S = Specific, M = Measurable, A = Attainable, R = Realistic, T = Time-bound.
ms: S = Khusus, M = Boleh diukur, A = Boleh dicapai, R = Realistik, T = Tempoh masa.

en: M = Measurable (Boleh diukur).
ms: M = Measurable (Boleh diukur).

question.en: Which of the following is a FIXED EXPENSE for a food stall operator?
question.ms: Antara berikut, yang manakah merupakan PERBELANJAAN TETAP bagi pengusaha gerai makanan?

feedback.en: Correct! Rent is fixed every month regardless of sales volume.
feedback.ms: Tepat! Sewa adalah tetap setiap bulan tanpa mengira jumlah jualan.

options.text: Cost of raw ingredients (Kos bahan mentah)

feedback.en: Ingredient cost varies depending on how many meals are prepared (variable).
feedback.ms: Kos bahan mentah berubah mengikut kuantiti masakan (boleh ubah).

feedback.en: Utility bills fluctuate each month (variable).
feedback.ms: Bil utiliti berubah setiap bulan (boleh ubah).

feedback.en: Packaging cost increases with more customer orders (variable).
feedback.ms: Kos bungkusan meningkat apabila pesanan bertambah (boleh ubah).

en: Fixed expenses remain constant every month regardless of production.
ms: Perbelanjaan tetap tidak berubah setiap bulan tanpa mengira pengeluaran.

en: Stall rent is a fixed monthly payment.
ms: Sewa gerai ialah bayaran tetap setiap bulan.

question.en: A stall owner deposits RM 5,000 in a fixed deposit account offering a simple interest rate of 3% per annum for 2 years. Calculate the total interest earned.
question.ms: Pemilik gerai mendepositkan RM 5,000 ke dalam akaun simpanan tetap dengan kadar faedah mudah 3% setahun selama 2 tahun. Hitung jumlah faedah yang diperoleh.

feedback.en: 150 is the interest for 1 year; multiply by 2 years.
feedback.ms: 150 ialah faedah 1 tahun; darabkan dengan 2 tahun.
3% ialah 0.03, bukan 0.003.

feedback.en: RM 5,300 is the total maturity value (P + I), not just the interest.
feedback.ms: RM 5,300 ialah jumlah matang (P + I), bukan faedah sahaja.

en: I = Prt where P = 5000, r = 0.03, t = 2.
ms: I = Prt dengan P = 5000, r = 0.03, t = 2.

question.en: Which of the following is considered PASSIVE INCOME for an entrepreneur?
question.ms: Antara berikut, yang manakah dianggap sebagai PENDAPATAN PASIF bagi seorang usahawan?

options.text: Rental income received from subletting a kitchen space

feedback.en: Correct! Rental income is earned with minimal active labor.
feedback.ms: Tepat! Pendapatan sewa diperoleh tanpa memerlukan tenaga buruh aktif harian.

feedback.en: Sales revenue requires active daily cooking and operation (active income).
feedback.ms: Hasil jualan harian memerlukan kerja memasak aktif (pendapatan aktif).

feedback.en: Wages for hours worked are active income.
feedback.ms: Upah mengikut jam ialah pendapatan aktif.

feedback.en: Tips are earned from active service work.
feedback.ms: Tip diperoleh daripada kerja perkhidmatan aktif.

en: Passive income is money earned regularly with little to no daily active effort (e.g. rent, dividends).
ms: Pendapatan pasif diperoleh secara berkala dengan usaha aktif harian yang minimum (cth: sewa, dividen).

en: Rental income is classified as passive income.
ms: Pendapatan sewa diklasifikasikan sebagai pendapatan pasif.

question.en: A chef wants to save RM 3,600 over 12 months to buy a commercial oven. How much must be saved each month?
question.ms: Seorang tukang masak ingin menyimpan RM 3,600 dalam tempoh 12 bulan untuk membeli ketuhar komersial. Berapakah jumlah yang mesti disimpan setiap bulan?

feedback.en: Correct! 3600 / 12 = RM 300 per month.
feedback.ms: Tepat! 3600 / 12 = RM 300 sebulan.

feedback.en: 3600 / 10 = 360, but time is 12 months.
feedback.ms: 3600 / 10 = 360, tetapi tempoh ialah 12 bulan.

en: Divide target amount (RM 3,600) by number of months (12).
ms: Bahagi sasaran wang (RM 3,600) dengan bilangan bulan (12).

en: Monthly savings = 3600 / 12 = RM 300.
ms: Simpanan bulanan = 3600 / 12 = RM 300.

question.en: A restaurant records total monthly income of RM 6,000, fixed expenses of RM 2,500, and variable expenses of RM 2,300. What is the net cash flow?
question.ms: Sebuah restoran merekodkan jumlah pendapatan bulanan RM 6,000, perbelanjaan tetap RM 2,500, dan perbelanjaan boleh ubah RM 2,300. Apakah aliran tunai bersih?

equation: Net Cash Flow = Income - Total Expenses

feedback.en: Correct! Total expenses = 2500 + 2300 = 4800. Net cash flow = 6000 - 4800 = +RM 1,200 (surplus).
feedback.ms: Tepat! Jumlah belanja = 4800. Aliran tunai bersih = 6000 - 4800 = +RM 1,200 (lebihan).

feedback.en: Income exceeds expenses, so it is a surplus, not a deficit.
feedback.ms: Pendapatan melebihi perbelanjaan, maka ia lebihan (surplus).

feedback.en: Remember to subtract variable expenses as well.
feedback.ms: Ingat untuk menolak perbelanjaan boleh ubah juga.

feedback.en: Remember to subtract fixed expenses.
feedback.ms: Ingat untuk menolak perbelanjaan tetap.

en: Total expenses = Fixed + Variable. Net cash flow = Income - Total expenses.
ms: Jumlah perbelanjaan = Tetap + Boleh ubah. Aliran tunai = Pendapatan - Jumlah perbelanjaan.

question.en: An investment of RM 10,000 earns 4% per annum compounded semi-annually (n = 2) for 3 years. What is the total accumulated amount? (Formula: A = P(1 + r/n)^(nt)).
question.ms: Pelaburan RM 10,000 memperoleh faedah 4% setahun dikompaun setiap setengah tahun (n = 2) selama 3 tahun. Apakah jumlah wang terkumpul? (Rumus: A = P(1 + r/n)^(nt)).

feedback.en: RM 11,200 is simple interest (10000 × 0.04 × 3 = 1200).
feedback.ms: RM 11,200 ialah faedah mudah, bukan kompaun.

feedback.en: Check calculation: (1.02)⁶ ≈ 1.126162.
feedback.ms: Semak pengiraan: (1.02)⁶ ≈ 1.126162.

feedback.en: Calculation error.
feedback.ms: Ralat pengiraan.

question.en: A credit card statement shows an outstanding balance of RM 3,200. The bank requires a minimum monthly payment of 5% of the balance or RM 50, whichever is higher. What is the minimum payment?
question.ms: Penyata kad kredit menunjukkan baki tertunggak sebanyak RM 3,200. Bank menetapkan bayaran minimum bulanan 5% daripada baki atau RM 50, yang mana lebih tinggi. Berapakah bayaran minimum?

feedback.en: Correct! 5% of 3200 = 0.05 × 3200 = RM 160, which is higher than RM 50.
feedback.ms: Tepat! 5% daripada 3200 = RM 160, yang lebih tinggi daripada RM 50.

feedback.en: 5% of balance (RM 160) exceeds the RM 50 minimum threshold.
feedback.ms: 5% daripada baki (RM 160) melebihi ambang minimum RM 50.

feedback.en: 320 is 10%, but the requirement is 5%.
feedback.ms: 320 ialah 10%, tetapi syarat ialah 5%.

en: Calculate 5% of RM 3,200: 0.05 × 3200 = RM 160. Compare with RM 50.
ms: Kira 5% daripada RM 3,200: 0.05 × 3200 = RM 160. Bandingkan dengan RM 50.

en: 5% of 3200 = RM 160 > RM 50. Minimum payment = RM 160.
ms: 5% daripada 3200 = RM 160 > RM 50. Bayaran minimum = RM 160.

question.en: A food vendor has total monthly living and operating expenses of RM 3,500. According to standard financial guidelines, what is the recommended minimum emergency fund (3 to 6 months of expenses)?
question.ms: Seorang peniaga makanan mempunyai jumlah perbelanjaan bulanan RM 3,500. Berdasarkan panduan kewangan standard, apakah cadangan dana kecemasan minimum (3 hingga 6 bulan perbelanjaan)?

feedback.en: This is only 2 to 4 months of expenses.
feedback.ms: Ini hanya 2 hingga 4 bulan perbelanjaan.

feedback.en: This is only 1 to 2 months of expenses.
feedback.ms: Ini hanya 1 hingga 2 bulan perbelanjaan.

feedback.en: This is 6 to 12 months.
feedback.ms: Ini ialah 6 hingga 12 bulan.

en: Multiply monthly expenses (RM 3,500) by 3 and by 6.
ms: Darabkan perbelanjaan bulanan (RM 3,500) dengan 3 dan dengan 6.

en: 3 months = RM 10,500. 6 months = RM 21,000.
ms: 3 bulan = RM 10,500. 6 bulan = RM 21,000.

question.en: A caterer earns a monthly net income of RM 4,500 and pays RM 1,800 in total monthly loan commitments. Calculate the Debt Service Ratio (DSR).
question.ms: Seorang katering memperoleh pendapatan bersih bulanan RM 4,500 dan membayar RM 1,800 dalam jumlah komitmen pinjaman bulanan. Hitung Nisbah Khidmat Hutang (DSR).

feedback.en: Check calculation: 18 / 45 = 2 / 5 = 40%.
feedback.ms: Semak pengiraan: 18 / 45 = 2 / 5 = 40%.

feedback.en: 40% is the exact ratio.
feedback.ms: 40% ialah nisbah tepat.

en: DSR = (Total monthly debt commitments ÷ Net income) × 100%.
ms: DSR = (Jumlah komitmen hutang bulanan ÷ Pendapatan bersih) × 100%.

question.en: A stall operator has net income RM 5,000, fixed expenses RM 2,800, and variable expenses RM 2,500 (deficit of RM 300). To achieve a monthly savings goal of RM 500, by how much must variable expenses be reduced?
question.ms: Pengusaha gerai mempunyai pendapatan bersih RM 5,000, perbelanjaan tetap RM 2,800, dan perbelanjaan boleh ubah RM 2,500 (defisit RM 300). Untuk mencapai matlamat simpanan RM 500 sebulan, berapakah jumlah perbelanjaan boleh ubah yang mesti dikurangkan?

feedback.en: Correct! Current deficit is RM 300. To reach +RM 500 surplus, expenses must be reduced by 300 + 500 = RM 800.
feedback.ms: Tepat! Defisit semasa RM 300. Untuk capai lebihan RM 500, belanja mesti dikurangkan sebanyak 300 + 500 = RM 800.

feedback.en: Reducing by RM 500 only leaves a surplus of RM 200 (since starting deficit was RM 300).
feedback.ms: Mengurangkan RM 500 hanya memberi lebihan RM 200 (kerana defisit awal RM 300).

feedback.en: Reducing by RM 300 brings cash flow to break-even (RM 0), not RM 500 savings.
feedback.ms: Mengurangkan RM 300 hanya mencapai titik pulang modal (RM 0).

feedback.en: RM 800 reduction achieves exactly RM 500 savings.
feedback.ms: Pengurangan RM 800 mencapai simpanan RM 500 tepat.

en: Current deficit = -RM 300. Target surplus = +RM 500. Total improvement needed = 500 - (-300) = RM 800.
ms: Defisit semasa = -RM 300. Lebihan sasaran = +RM 500. Jumlah penjimatan diperlukan = 500 - (-300) = RM 800.

en: Target variable expenses = 5000 - 2800 - 500 = RM 1,700. Reduction = 2500 - 1700 = RM 800.
ms: Sasaran belanja boleh ubah = 5000 - 2800 - 500 = RM 1,700. Pengurangan = 2500 - 1700 = RM 800.

question.en: A delivery van loan of RM 40,000 has a flat interest rate of 3% per annum for 5 years. Calculate the total repayment amount and the monthly installment.
question.ms: Pinjaman van penghantaran sebanyak RM 40,000 mempunyai kadar faedah sama rata 3% setahun selama 5 tahun. Hitung jumlah bayaran balik dan ansuran bulanan.

feedback.en: Correct! Total interest = 40000 × 0.03 × 5 = RM 6,000. Total = RM 46,000. Monthly = 46000 / 60 = RM 766.67.
feedback.ms: Tepat! Faedah = RM 6,000. Jumlah = RM 46,000. Ansuran = 46000 / 60 = RM 766.67.

feedback.en: RM 1,200 is interest for only 1 year, not 5 years.
feedback.ms: RM 1,200 ialah faedah 1 tahun sahaja, bukan 5 tahun.

feedback.en: 5 years is 60 months, not 50 months.
feedback.ms: 5 tahun bersamaan 60 bulan, bukan 50 bulan.
Faedah ialah RM 6,000.

en: Total interest I = Prt = 40000 × 0.03 × 5 = 6000. Total A = 46000. Divide by 60 months.
ms: Faedah I = Prt = 40000 × 0.03 × 5 = 6000. Jumlah A = 46000. Bahagi 60 bulan.

en: Total repayment = RM 46,000. Monthly installment = 46000 / 60 = RM 766.67.
ms: Jumlah bayaran balik = RM 46,000. Ansuran bulanan = 46000 / 60 = RM 766.67.

question.en: An unpaid credit card balance of RM 2,000 incurs a finance charge of 18% per annum. What is the finance charge for 30 days? (Use 365 days in a year).
question.ms: Baki kad kredit tertunggak sebanyak RM 2,000 dikenakan caj kewangan 18% setahun. Apakah caj kewangan untuk tempoh 30 hari? (Gunakan 365 hari dalam setahun).

feedback.en: Using 360 days gives 30.00, but standard banking uses 365 days (RM 29.59).
feedback.ms: Menggunakan 360 hari memberi 30.00, perbankan standard menggunakan 365 hari (RM 29.59).

feedback.en: 36.00 is for 0.1 of a year (36.5 days).
feedback.ms: 36.00 adalah bagi 36.5 hari.

feedback.en: Calculation error.
feedback.ms: Ralat pengiraan.

en: Charge = Balance × (Rate/100) × (Days / 365).
ms: Caj = Baki × (Kadar/100) × (Hari / 365).

question.en: An investment portfolio for restaurant renovation earned a nominal return of 7.5% over the past year. If the inflation rate was 3.2%, what was the approximate real rate of return?
question.ms: Portfolio pelaburan untuk pengubahsuaian restoran memperoleh pulangan nominal 7.5% sepanjang tahun lepas. Jika kadar inflasi ialah 3.2%, apakah anggaran kadar pulangan sebenar?

equation: Real Rate ≈ Nominal Rate - Inflation Rate

feedback.en: Correct! Real rate ≈ 7.5% - 3.2% = 4.3%.
feedback.ms: Tepat! Kadar sebenar ≈ 7.5% - 3.2% = 4.3%.

feedback.en: Inflation erodes purchasing power; subtract inflation, do not add it.
feedback.ms: Inflasi menghakis kuasa beli; tolak inflasi, jangan tambah.

feedback.en: 7.5 / 3.2 is not the formula.
feedback.ms: 7.5 / 3.2 bukan rumus pulangan sebenar.

en: Real Rate of Return ≈ Nominal Return - Inflation Rate.
ms: Kadar Pulangan Sebenar ≈ Pulangan Nominal - Kadar Inflasi.
Kadar sebenar = 7.5% - 3.2% = 4.3%.

question.en: A food stall incurs fixed startup equipment costs of RM 12,000. Each dish sold generates a net contribution margin of RM 4. If the stall sells an average of 100 dishes per day, in how many days will it break even?
question.ms: Sebuah gerai makanan menanggung kos permulaan peralatan tetap sebanyak RM 12,000. Setiap hidangan yang dijual menjana margin caruman bersih RM 4. Jika gerai menjual purata 100 hidangan sehari, dalam berapa harikah ia akan mencapai titik pulang modal?

feedback.en: Correct! Daily margin = 100 × RM 4 = RM 400. Break-even days = 12000 / 400 = 30 days.
feedback.ms: Tepat! Margin harian = 100 × RM 4 = RM 400. Hari pulang modal = 12000 / 400 = 30 hari.

feedback.en: 30 days is the exact break-even timeline.
feedback.ms: 30 hari ialah garis masa pulang modal yang tepat.

en: Daily contribution = 100 dishes × RM 4 = RM 400/day. Days = 12,000 / 400.
ms: Caruman harian = 100 hidangan × RM 4 = RM 400/hari. Hari = 12,000 / 400.

question.en: In the SMART financial goal concept, what does the letter 'M' stand for?
question.ms: Dalam konsep matlamat kewangan SMART, apakah yang diwakili oleh huruf 'M'?

text.en: Measurable (Boleh diukur)

feedback.en: Correct! SMART = Specific, Measurable, Attainable, Realistic, Time-bound.
feedback.ms: Tepat! SMART = Khusus (S), Boleh diukur (M), Boleh dicapai (A), Bersifat realistik (R), Tempoh masa (T).

text.en: Manageable (Boleh diurus)

feedback.en: M stands for Measurable.
feedback.ms: M ialah untuk Boleh diukur (Measurable).

text.en: Monetary (Berasaskan wang)

feedback.en: M stands for Measurable.
feedback.ms: M bermaksud Measurable.

text.en: Monthly (Bulanan)

feedback.en: M stands for Measurable.
feedback.ms: M bermaksud Measurable.

en: S = Specific, M = Measurable, A = Attainable, R = Realistic, T = Time-bound.
ms: S = Khusus, M = Boleh diukur, A = Boleh dicapai, R = Realistik, T = Tempoh masa.

en: M stands for Measurable: The financial goal must have a quantifiable numerical target.
ms: M mewakili Measurable (Boleh diukur): Matlamat kewangan mesti mempunyai sasaran angka yang boleh diukur.

question.en: Which of the following is considered a fixed expense for Warung Mama?
question.ms: Antara berikut, yang manakah merupakan perbelanjaan tetap bagi Warung Mama?

text.en: Monthly shop rental of RM 1,200

feedback.en: Correct! Shop rental is fixed every month regardless of sales volume.
feedback.ms: Tepat! Sewa kedai adalah tetap setiap bulan tanpa mengira jumlah jualan.

text.en: Purchase of chicken and rice for cooking
text.ms: Pembelian ayam dan beras untuk memasak

feedback.en: Ingredient costs vary with customer volume (variable expense).
feedback.ms: Kos bahan mentah berubah mengikut jumlah pelanggan (perbelanjaan tidak tetap).

text.en: Electricity bill based on usage

feedback.en: Utility bills fluctuate each month (variable expense).
feedback.ms: Bil utiliti berubah mengikut penggunaan (perbelanjaan tidak tetap).

text.en: Cost of cooking gas cylinders used
text.ms: Kos tong gas memasak yang digunakan

feedback.en: Cooking gas cost depends on cooking frequency (variable).
feedback.ms: Kos gas memasak bergantung pada kekerapan memasak (tidak tetap).

en: Fixed expenses are costs that must be paid regularly with an unchanging amount (e.g. rent).
ms: Perbelanjaan tetap ialah kos yang mesti dibayar secara berkala dengan amaun yang tidak berubah (cth. sewa kedai).

en: Shop rental is a predetermined constant amount paid every month, classifying it as a fixed expense.
ms: Sewa kedai ialah bayaran tetap setiap bulan yang tidak bergantung pada tahap perniagaan, menjadikannya perbelanjaan tetap.

question.en: What happens when a person's total monthly income exceeds total monthly expenses?
question.ms: Apakah yang berlaku apabila jumlah pendapatan bulanan seseorang melebihi jumlah perbelanjaan bulatannya?

text.en: Positive cash flow (surplus)

feedback.en: Correct! Income greater than expenses generates a positive cash flow.
feedback.ms: Tepat! Pendapatan melebihi perbelanjaan menghasilkan aliran tunai positif.

text.en: Negative cash flow (deficit)

feedback.en: Negative cash flow occurs when expenses exceed income.
feedback.ms: Aliran tunai negatif berlaku apabila perbelanjaan melebihi pendapatan.

text.en: Bankruptcy

feedback.en: Surplus increases financial security, not bankruptcy.
feedback.ms: Lebihan tunai mengukuhkan kewangan, bukan muflis.

text.en: Zero net worth

feedback.en: Net worth improves with positive cash flow.
feedback.ms: Nilai bersih meningkat dengan aliran tunai positif.

en: Income > Expenses = Surplus (positive cash flow).
ms: Pendapatan > Perbelanjaan = Lebihan (aliran tunai positif).

en: When Total Income - Total Expenses > 0, it is defined as a positive cash flow.
ms: Apabila Jumlah Pendapatan - Jumlah Perbelanjaan > 0, ia ditakrifkan sebagai aliran tunai positif.

question.en: Which of the following is an example of passive income for Mama?
question.ms: Antara berikut, yang manakah merupakan contoh pendapatan pasif bagi Mama?

text.en: Rental received from leasing out a food stall space
text.ms: Sewa yang diterima daripada menyewakan ruang gerai makanan

feedback.en: Correct! Rental income is earned with minimal ongoing labor (passive income).
feedback.ms: Tepat! Pendapatan sewa diperoleh tanpa perlu bekerja setiap hari (pendapatan pasif).

text.en: Sales revenue from cooking Nasi Lemak daily
text.ms: Hasil jualan daripada memasak Nasi Lemak setiap hari

feedback.en: This requires daily manual work (active income).
feedback.ms: Ini memerlukan tenaga kerja harian (pendapatan aktif).

text.en: Tips received directly from serving dining customers
text.ms: Tip yang diterima terus daripada melayan pelanggan

feedback.en: Tips are earned from active service.
feedback.ms: Tip diperoleh daripada perkhidmatan aktif.

text.en: Overtime cooking pay

feedback.en: Overtime pay is active income.
feedback.ms: Gaji lebih masa ialah pendapatan aktif.

en: Passive income is money earned from investments or property that doesn't require active daily work.
ms: Pendapatan pasif ialah wang yang diperoleh daripada pelaburan atau hartanah tanpa perlu bekerja aktif setiap hari.

en: Rental income from leased property is classified as passive income.
ms: Pendapatan sewa daripada hartanah yang disewakan diklasifikasikan sebagai pendapatan pasif.

question.en: Financial planners generally recommend having an emergency fund equivalent to at least how many months of basic living expenses?
question.ms: Perancang kewangan lazimnya mengesyorkan simpanan dana kecemasan sekurang-kurangnya berapa bulan perbelanjaan asas hidup?

equation: Emergency fund / Dana kecemasan: 3 to 6 months

text.en: 3 to 6 months

feedback.en: Correct! An emergency fund should cover 3 to 6 months of essential living expenses.
feedback.ms: Tepat! Dana kecemasan sepatutnya menampung 3 hingga 6 bulan perbelanjaan asas hidup.

text.en: 1 to 2 weeks

feedback.en: A few weeks is too short to protect against major emergencies.
feedback.ms: Beberapa minggu terlalu singkat untuk melindungi daripada kecemasan utama.

text.en: 5 to 10 years

feedback.en: That is long-term retirement savings, not an emergency fund.
feedback.ms: Itu simpanan persaraan jangka panjang, bukan dana kecemasan.

text.en: Exactly 1 month

feedback.en: One month is insufficient for unexpected disruptions.
feedback.ms: Satu bulan tidak mencukupi untuk gangguan luar jangka.

en: Standard Form 4 syllabus guideline: 3 to 6 months of basic expenses.
ms: Garis panduan sukatan Tingkatan 4: 3 hingga 6 bulan perbelanjaan asas.

en: An emergency fund of 3 to 6 months of essential expenses provides a safety net during job loss or medical crises.
ms: Dana kecemasan sebanyak 3 hingga 6 bulan perbelanjaan asas menyediakan jaring keselamatan sekiranya berlaku kehilangan pendapatan atau krisis perubatan.

question.en: Mama wants to buy a modern high-capacity food steamer costing RM 3,600 in 10 months. How much must Mama save each month to achieve this SMART goal?
question.ms: Mama ingin membeli pengukus makanan berkapasiti tinggi moden berharga RM 3,600 dalam tempoh 10 bulan. Berapakah yang mesti disimpan oleh Mama setiap bulan untuk mencapai matlamat SMART ini?

feedback.en: Correct! Monthly savings = RM 3,600 / 10 = RM 360.
feedback.ms: Tepat! Simpanan bulanan = RM 3,600 / 10 = RM 360.

feedback.en: RM 300 * 10 = RM 3,000, which is RM 600 short.
feedback.ms: RM 300 * 10 = RM 3,000, kurang RM 600.

en: Divide total target price by number of months.
ms: Bahagikan harga sasaran dengan bilangan bulan.

en: Required monthly savings = RM 3,600 / 10 months = RM 360 per month.
ms: Simpanan bulanan yang diperlukan = RM 3,600 / 10 bulan = RM 360 sebulan.

question.en: Encik Razak has a monthly salary of RM 4,500 and rental income of RM 500. His fixed expenses are RM 2,200 and variable expenses are RM 1,800. What is his net monthly cash flow?
question.ms: Encik Razak mempunyai gaji bulanan RM 4,500 dan pendapatan sewa RM 500. Perbelanjaan tetapnya ialah RM 2,200 dan perbelanjaan tidak tetap ialah RM 1,800. Apakah aliran tunai bersih bulanannya?

feedback.en: Correct! Total income = RM 5,000. Total expenses = RM 4,000. Cash flow = 5,000 - 4,000 = RM +1,000.
feedback.ms: Tepat! Jumlah pendapatan = RM 5,000. Jumlah perbelanjaan = RM 4,000. Aliran tunai = RM +1,000 (Lebihan).

feedback.en: Don't forget to include the rental income of RM 500.
feedback.ms: Jangan lupa masukkan pendapatan sewa RM 500.

feedback.en: Income exceeds expenses, so cash flow is positive.
feedback.ms: Pendapatan melebihi perbelanjaan, jadi aliran tunai positif.

feedback.en: Recalculate 5000 - 4000.
feedback.ms: Kira semula 5000 - 4000.

en: Total income = 4500 + 500 = 5000. Total expenses = 2200 + 1800 = 4000.
ms: Jumlah pendapatan = 4500 + 500 = 5000. Jumlah perbelanjaan = 2200 + 1800 = 4000.

en: Net Cash Flow = Total Income (RM 5,000) - Total Expenses (RM 4,000) = RM +1,000 (Surplus).
ms: Aliran Tunai Bersih = Jumlah Pendapatan (RM 5,000) - Jumlah Perbelanjaan (RM 4,000) = RM +1,000 (Lebihan).

question.en: Puan Halimah has monthly fixed expenses of RM 1,800 and essential variable expenses of RM 1,200. What is the recommended minimum emergency fund (3 months)?
question.ms: Puan Halimah mempunyai perbelanjaan tetap bulanan RM 1,800 dan perbelanjaan tidak tetap asas RM 1,200. Apakah dana kecemasan minimum yang disyorkan (3 bulan)?

feedback.en: Correct! Monthly basic expenses = 1,800 + 1,200 = RM 3,000. For 3 months = 3 * 3,000 = RM 9,000.
feedback.ms: Tepat! Perbelanjaan bulanan = RM 3,000. Untuk 3 bulan = 3 * 3,000 = RM 9,000.

feedback.en: RM 5,400 only covers fixed expenses for 3 months (3 * 1800).
feedback.ms: RM 5,400 hanya menampung perbelanjaan tetap (3 * 1800).

feedback.en: RM 6,000 is for 2 months.
feedback.ms: RM 6,000 ialah untuk 2 bulan.

feedback.en: RM 18,000 is for 6 months (the upper recommended limit).
feedback.ms: RM 18,000 ialah untuk 6 bulan (had maksimum yang disyorkan).

en: Add monthly expenses first (RM 1,800 + RM 1,200 = RM 3,000), then multiply by 3.
ms: Jumlahkan perbelanjaan bulanan dahulu (RM 1,800 + RM 1,200 = RM 3,000), kemudian darab 3.

en: Basic monthly expenses = RM 3,000. 3-month emergency fund = 3 × RM 3,000 = RM 9,000.
ms: Perbelanjaan asas bulanan = RM 3,000. Dana kecemasan 3 bulan = 3 × RM 3,000 = RM 9,000.

question.en: In financial planning, which of the following is categorized as a LONG-TERM financial goal?
question.ms: Dalam perancangan kewangan, antara berikut yang manakah dikategorikan sebagai matlamat kewangan JANGKA PANJANG?

text.en: Accumulating a child's university education fund in 12 years
text.ms: Mengumpul dana pendidikan universiti anak dalam tempoh 12 tahun

feedback.en: Correct! Goals with a timeframe exceeding 5 years are long-term goals.
feedback.ms: Tepat! Matlamat dengan tempoh melebihi 5 tahun ialah matlamat jangka panjang.

text.en: Saving RM 2,000 for a holiday next month
text.ms: Menyimpan RM 2,000 untuk percutian bulan hadapan

feedback.en: This is a short-term goal (< 1 year).
feedback.ms: Ini ialah matlamat jangka pendek (< 1 tahun).

text.en: Buying a new refrigerator in 6 months
text.ms: Membeli peti sejuk baharu dalam tempoh 6 bulan

feedback.en: This is a short-term goal.
feedback.ms: Ini matlamat jangka pendek.

text.en: Paying off an annual insurance premium in 1 year
text.ms: Membayar premium insurans tahunan dalam tempoh 1 tahun

feedback.en: This is a short-term goal.
feedback.ms: Ini matlamat jangka pendek.

en: Short-term goals: less than 1 year. Long-term goals: more than 5 years.
ms: Matlamat jangka pendek: kurang 1 tahun. Matlamat jangka panjang: melebihi 5 tahun.

en: Saving for a university degree 12 years in the future exceeds 5 years, classifying it as a long-term goal.
ms: Simpanan untuk pendidikan universiti 12 tahun akan datang melebihi 5 tahun, menjadikannya matlamat jangka panjang.

question.en: If a person faces a monthly financial deficit (negative cash flow), what is the best immediate action to take?
question.ms: Jika seseorang menghadapi defisit kewangan bulanan (aliran tunai negatif), apakah tindakan segera terbaik yang perlu diambil?

text.en: Reduce discretionary variable expenses and look for additional active/passive income
text.ms: Mengurangkan perbelanjaan tidak tetap kehendak dan mencari pendapatan tambahan

feedback.en: Correct! Cutting non-essential spending and increasing income turns deficit into surplus.
feedback.ms: Tepat! Memotong perbelanjaan bukan keperluan dan menambah pendapatan menukar defisit kepada lebihan.

text.en: Take an expensive personal loan to cover the deficit
text.ms: Mengambil pinjaman peribadi faedah tinggi untuk menampung defisit

feedback.en: High interest debt increases future financial burden.
feedback.ms: Hutang faedah tinggi meningkatkan beban kewangan masa depan.

text.en: Stop paying fixed housing loan installments
text.ms: Berhenti membayar ansuran pinjaman perumahan tetap

feedback.en: Defaulting on housing loan leads to foreclosure.
feedback.ms: Gagal bayar pinjaman rumah mengakibatkan rumah disita.

text.en: Double variable expenses to boost lifestyle
text.ms: Menggandakan perbelanjaan tidak tetap untuk gaya hidup

feedback.en: This would worsen the deficit.
feedback.ms: Ini akan memburukkan defisit.

en: To fix negative cash flow: either reduce variable expenses, increase income, or both.
ms: Untuk membaiki aliran tunai negatif: kurangkan perbelanjaan tidak tetap, tambah pendapatan, atau kedua-duanya.

en: Managing a deficit requires trimming non-essential variable spending and finding secondary sources of income.
ms: Mengurus defisit memerlukan pengurangan perbelanjaan tidak tetap kehendak dan mencari punca pendapatan sampingan.

question.en: Uncle Muthu earns RM 3,200 monthly with expenses of RM 2,700. He sets a goal: 'Save RM 12,000 in 18 months for stall renovation'. Is this financial goal realistic (Achievable under SMART)?
question.ms: Uncle Muthu berpendapatan RM 3,200 sebulan dengan perbelanjaan RM 2,700. Beliau menetapkan matlamat: 'Menyimpan RM 12,000 dalam 18 bulan untuk renovasi gerai'. Adakah matlamat kewangan ini realistik (Boleh dicapai di bawah SMART)?

text.en: No, because he needs RM 666.67 monthly but his surplus is only RM 500
text.ms: Tidak, kerana beliau memerlukan RM 666.67 sebulan tetapi lebihan tunainya hanya RM 500

feedback.en: Correct! Required savings = 12,000 / 18 = RM 666.67. Monthly surplus = 3,200 - 2,700 = RM 500. The deficit is RM 166.67/month.
feedback.ms: Tepat! Simpanan diperlukan = RM 666.67 sebulan. Lebihan tunai hanya RM 500 sebulan. Matlamat tidak realistik tanpa mengurangkan perbelanjaan.

text.en: Yes, because 18 months is a long period
text.ms: Ya, kerana 18 bulan tempoh yang lama

feedback.en: Total accumulated at RM 500/month is only RM 9,000, short of RM 12,000.
feedback.ms: Jumlah simpanan hanya RM 9,000 (18 x 500), kurang daripada RM 12,000.

text.en: Yes, because his salary is RM 3,200

feedback.en: Salary must be evaluated against expenses.
feedback.ms: Gaji mesti dinilai bersama perbelanjaan.

text.en: Cannot be evaluated

feedback.en: Calculations give a definitive answer.
feedback.ms: Pengiraan memberikan jawapan muktamad.

en: Required monthly savings = 12,000 / 18 = RM 666.67. Current monthly savings = 3,200 - 2,700 = RM 500.
ms: Simpanan bulanan diperlukan = 12,000 / 18 = RM 666.67. Simpanan bulanan semasa = 3,200 - 2,700 = RM 500.

en: Uncle Muthu can only save RM 500 per month (RM 9,000 in 18 months). He needs RM 666.67/month. Thus, the goal is not realistic unless expenses are reduced or income increased.
ms: Uncle Muthu hanya mampu menyimpan RM 500 sebulan (RM 9,000 dalam 18 bulan). Beliau memerlukan RM 666.67 sebulan. Maka matlamat ini tidak realistik kecuali perbelanjaan dikurangkan atau pendapatan ditambah.

question.en: Siti wants to buy an apartment priced at RM 250,000. She needs a 10% down payment. If Siti saves RM 625 every month, how many years will it take her to save the full down payment?
question.ms: Siti ingin membeli sebuah apartmen berharga RM 250,000. Beliau memerlukan 10% wang pendahuluan. Jika Siti menyimpan RM 625 setiap bulan, berapakah bilangan tahun yang diperlukannya untuk mengumpul wang pendahuluan tersebut sepenuhnya?

feedback.en: Correct! Down payment = RM 25,000. Number of months = 25,000 / 625 = 40 months = 3 years 4 months.
feedback.ms: Tepat! Wang pendahuluan = RM 25,000. Bilangan bulan = 25,000 / 625 = 40 bulan = 3 tahun 4 bulan.

feedback.en: 48 * 625 = RM 30,000, which exceeds the needed RM 25,000.

en: 10% of RM 250,000 is RM 25,000. Divide RM 25,000 by RM 625.
ms: 10% daripada RM 250,000 ialah RM 25,000. Bahagikan RM 25,000 dengan RM 625.

en: 10% of RM 250,000 = RM 25,000. Months required = 25,000 / 625 = 40 months = 3 years 4 months.
ms: 10% daripada RM 250,000 = RM 25,000. Masa diperlukan = 25,000 / 625 = 40 bulan = 3 tahun 4 bulan.

question.en:
Mama's monthly financial report shows:
Net Active Income: RM 4,800
Passive Income: RM 600
Fixed Expenses: RM 2,100
Variable Expenses: RM 1,900
Monthly Investment in Unit Trust: RM 400
What is Mama's final remaining surplus cash flow at month-end?
question.ms:
Laporan kewangan bulanan Mama menunjukkan:
Pendapatan Aktif Bersih: RM 4,800
Pendapatan Pasif: RM 600
Perbelanjaan Tetap: RM 2,100
Perbelanjaan Tidak Tetap: RM 1,900
Pelaburan Bulanan Unit Amanah: RM 400
Apakah baki lebihan aliran tunai Mama pada akhir bulan?

feedback.en: Correct! Total inflows = 4,800 + 600 = RM 5,400. Total outflows = 2,100 + 1,900 + 400 = RM 4,400. Surplus = 5,400 - 4,400 = RM 1,000.
feedback.ms: Tepat! Jumlah pendapatan = RM 5,400. Jumlah aliran keluar = RM 4,400. Lebihan = RM 1,000.

feedback.en: Remember to deduct the monthly investment (RM 400) from the surplus cash.
feedback.ms: Ingat tolak pelaburan bulanan (RM 400) daripada baki tunai.

feedback.en: Recalculate 5,400 - 4,400.
feedback.ms: Kira semula 5,400 - 4,400.

feedback.en: Check your income addition.
feedback.ms: Semak jumlah pendapatan.

en: Total income = 4800 + 600 = 5400. Total outflows = 2100 + 1900 + 400 = 4400.
ms: Jumlah pendapatan = 4800 + 600 = 5400. Jumlah perbelanjaan & pelaburan = 2100 + 1900 + 400 = 4400.

en: Total inflows = RM 5,400. Total outflows = RM 4,400. Net surplus = 5,400 - 4,400 = RM 1,000.
ms: Jumlah aliran masuk = RM 5,400. Jumlah aliran keluar = RM 4,400. Lebihan bersih = RM 1,000.

question.en: A warung equipment package currently costs RM 5,000. Due to 4% annual inflation, its price next year will be RM 5,000 × (1 + 0.04) = RM 5,200. If Mama saves RM 5,000 in a zero-interest tin over the year, how much extra must Mama add to purchase it?
question.ms: Satu pakej peralatan warung kini berharga RM 5,000. Disebabkan kadar inflasi 4% setahun, harganya tahun hadapan ialah RM 5,000 × (1 + 0.04) = RM 5,200. Jika Mama menyimpan RM 5,000 di dalam tabung tanpa faedah sepanjang tahun itu, berapakah wang tambahan yang perlu ditambah oleh Mama untuk membelinya?

feedback.en: Correct! The price rose to RM 5,200. Savings are RM 5,000. Shortfall = RM 5,200 - RM 5,000 = RM 200.
feedback.ms: Tepat! Harga meningkat ke RM 5,200. Simpanan ialah RM 5,000. Kekurangan = RM 200.
4% daripada 5,000 ialah 200, bukan 500.
4% daripada 5000 ialah 200.

feedback.en: Inflation increases the price above the original RM 5,000.
feedback.ms: Inflasi menaikkan harga melebihi RM 5,000 asal.

en: 4% inflation increases the price by 0.04 × 5000 = RM 200.
ms: Inflasi 4% menaikkan harga sebanyak 0.04 × 5000 = RM 200.

en: New price = RM 5,200. Amount in savings = RM 5,000. Shortfall due to inflation = RM 200.
ms: Harga baharu = RM 5,200. Simpanan sedia ada = RM 5,000. Kekurangan akibat inflasi = RM 200.

question.en: Which statement best adheres to ALL five SMART criteria for a financial goal?
question.ms: Pernyataan manakah yang paling menepati KELIMA-LIMA kriteria SMART bagi suatu matlamat kewangan?

text.en: Save RM 6,000 by depositing RM 500 every month for 12 months into a high-yield account for stall expansion
text.ms: Menyimpan RM 6,000 dengan memasukkan RM 500 setiap bulan selama 12 bulan ke dalam akaun hasil tinggi untuk pembesaran gerai

feedback.en: Correct! Specific (stall expansion), Measurable (RM 6,000), Attainable & Realistic (RM 500/month), Time-bound (12 months).
feedback.ms: Tepat! Khusus (pembesaran gerai), Boleh diukur (RM 6,000), Boleh dicapai & Realistik (RM 500/bulan), Berjangka masa (12 bulan).

text.en: Save a lot of money as soon as possible

feedback.en: Vague: not specific, not measurable, and no timeframe.
feedback.ms: Kabur: tidak khusus, tidak boleh diukur, dan tiada tempoh masa.

text.en: Become a billionaire in 3 months

feedback.en: Unrealistic and unattainable.
feedback.ms: Tidak realistik dan mustahil dicapai.

text.en: Save RM 10,000 someday
text.ms: Menyimpan RM 10,000 pada suatu hari nanti

feedback.en: Lacks a specific timeframe (not time-bound).
feedback.ms: Tiada tempoh masa (tidak berjangka masa).

en: A SMART goal has clear target amount, method, purpose, and deadline.
ms: Matlamat SMART mempunyai amaun sasaran, kaedah, tujuan, dan tarikh akhir yang jelas.

en: Option A fulfills all SMART criteria: Specific (stall expansion), Measurable (RM 6,000), Attainable (RM 500/month), Realistic, and Time-bound (12 months).
ms: Pilihan A memenuhi semua kriteria SMART: Khusus (pembesaran gerai), Boleh diukur (RM 6,000), Boleh dicapai (RM 500/bulan), Realistik, dan Berjangka masa (12 bulan).
